headline: Anthropic and OpenAI have sought significant control over what outside safety evaluators can publish about their AI models, Reuters reports, citing two people familiar with the talks.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: a Reuters exclusive on live talks over AI safety oversight, but it rests on two unnamed sources and both companies dispute parts of it.
importance_line: Anyone who relies on outside safety checks of powerful AI, from the public to regulators, is affected first, then the evaluators and the labs, because the talks will help decide how such models are scrutinised, but the account rests on two unnamed sources and both companies dispute parts of it.
summary: Reuters reports in an exclusive, citing two people familiar with the discussions, that Anthropic and OpenAI have sought significant control over what evaluators working inside their companies can publish, fearing trade secrets could leak, and that as recently as 5 Oct both wanted strict editorial control. Anthropic says this does not describe all its discussions, OpenAI says it is not seeking approval rights over the full text of reports, and Reuters adds that OpenAI redacted non-public information from an outside report on a hack of the AI platform Hugging Face set off by agents running on its models.
notes: Reuters site returned HTTP 401; the text was read in AOL.ca's carried copy of the Reuters wire, and the Reuters link is kept. Source credited to Reuters. The story could also fit SEC (AI safety); kept RES as set by the chunk.
